reasoning_traces.think:
The Two-Wave DFS architecture operates on a dual logic: first, simulating game dynamics via snap-by-snap trajectories to derive player projections; second, evaluating lineup performance against a modeled opponent field. The core insight is that GPP success hinges on beating the right tail of the opponent distribution, not maximizing expected value. This is formalized through Dirichlet-Multinomial modeling of field ownership, which captures both randomness and strategic behavior. The heavy-juice firewall prevents overexposure to market inefficiencies, while the 6-stage conjunction gate ensures only high-confidence, multi-source validated edges proceed. The simulation engine computes extreme quantiles (e.g., CVaR0.99) to optimize for rare but impactful outcomes. The submodular portfolio construction then selects lineups that maximize marginal coverage of top finishes, leveraging combinatorial optimization principles.
